paragraphs: Stochastic approximation algorithms improve an estimate through repeated updates affected by randomness. Averaging those estimates, rather than using only the latest one, is a well-established way to improve long-run statistical behavior. This paper asks a more immediate question: after a finite number of updates, how large could the averaged estimate’s error be with a specified level of confidence?

The authors develop a general framework that converts concentration bounds for individual, unaveraged iterates into a sharp concentration bound for their average. Access to those individual bounds is an explicit requirement of the approach. They also construct an example showing that their general result cannot be improved beyond constant multiplicative factors.

The framework yields tight bounds for contractive stochastic approximation and for averaged versions of temporal difference learning and Q-learning. Its significance is a reusable route from understanding individual updates to understanding averaging, including settings where direct analysis is difficult. These are finite-run probability guarantees, complementing the established asymptotic benefits of averaging.
neurips-2025-a-general-purpose-theorem-f.tldr: A general theorem turns concentration bounds for individual stochastic approximation iterates into sharp finite-run guarantees for their averages.

paragraphs: The paper studies finite-horizon restless bandits with N homogeneous arms. A common planning approach replaces random system behavior with its average evolution and solves a linear program. Under a non-degeneracy condition, policies from this fluid approximation can be extremely close to optimal. In degenerate problems, however, their per-arm optimality gap can instead scale as one over the square root of N.

The authors construct a Gaussian approximation that represents both the mean evolution and its variance. This gives the planner information about fluctuations that the fluid approximation omits. They then solve a stochastic program for this approximate system to obtain a policy.

Under a uniqueness assumption, the proposed policy achieves an optimality gap of order one over N, up to logarithmic factors, for degenerate problems. The abstract identifies this as the first such result. The contribution is therefore a conditional theoretical improvement: explicitly accounting for variability can sharpen policy guarantees in a setting where planning around the mean can be insufficient.
neurips-2025-achieving-tilde-mathcal-o-1.tldr: A Gaussian approximation enables a stochastic-programming policy with a near-1/N optimality gap for degenerate restless bandits under a uniqueness assumption.

paragraphs: Multi-view learning combines several descriptions of the same samples, but some descriptions may be missing. In graph-based semi-supervised learning, labels spread through similarity connections. The authors argue that ignoring missing samples can sometimes fragment local structure into sub-clusters, disrupting the smoothness assumption behind label propagation and distorting how graphs from different views are combined.

Their method, AGF-TI, addresses this through adversarial graph fusion and tensor-based reconstruction. A min-max formulation learns a consensus graph that resists distorted local structure. Stacking similarity matrices into a tensor lets the method use higher-order agreement across views, with low-rank tensor learning recovering incomplete relationships.

An anchor-based strategy reduces computational complexity, and an alternating optimization procedure incorporates reduced gradient descent. The authors establish convergence for the optimization and report better classification results than state-of-the-art methods across multiple datasets. The approach matters because it treats missing views as a potential structural disruption, combining robust fusion with reconstruction instead of relying solely on relationships that remain visible.
neurips-2025-adversarial-graph-fusion-fo.tldr: AGF-TI combines adversarial graph fusion and low-rank tensor reconstruction to address structural fragmentation caused by missing views.

paragraphs: Differentiable vector graphics allow a system to adjust curves using feedback from a rendered image. Existing representations can be expensive to optimize, particularly when seeking detailed results at high resolution. Bézier Splatting introduces a representation intended to make both rendering and the computation of optimization gradients faster while preserving visual quality.

The method places two-dimensional Gaussians along Bézier curves and renders them through splatting. These Gaussian samples naturally provide positional gradients at object boundaries, helping optimization determine how curve positions should change. An adaptive pruning and densification procedure also changes the spatial distribution of curves to help escape local minima and improve the resulting graphics.

For open curves, the authors report forward rasterization steps that are 30 times faster and backward steps that are 150 times faster than DiffVG. Experiments also show improved visual fidelity and optimization speed. Conversion to standard SVG connects the representation to existing vector graphics tools, making the proposed rendering approach useful beyond its own optimization pipeline.
neurips-2025-bezier-splatting-for-fast-a.tldr: Bézier Splatting renders Gaussian samples along curves to accelerate differentiable vector graphics optimization while improving visual fidelity.

paragraphs: Biological sequence generation benefits from dependencies that extend in both directions across a sequence. Autoregressive models generate sequentially, limiting their access to this global context. Non-autoregressive models can learn bidirectional representations, but face difficulties with coherent generation and scalability. This paper combines the two approaches so sequential generation can draw on richer biological context.

A shared input encoder feeds two decoders. The non-autoregressive decoder learns latent bidirectional features, while the autoregressive decoder generates the sequence. Cross-decoder attention allows the generating decoder to repeatedly query those features. Training uses importance annealing to balance objectives and blocks gradients across decoders to support stable, focused learning.

On a nine-species benchmark for de novo peptide sequencing, the authors report substantial improvements over both autoregressive and non-autoregressive baselines. They also report strong performance on diverse downstream data. The central contribution is an architecture that brings bidirectional information into autoregressive prediction through a separate learned representation, preserving the sequential decoder’s role in producing a coherent output.
neurips-2025-bidirectional-representatio.tldr: A hybrid biological sequence model improves autoregressive generation by letting it attend to bidirectional features learned by a second decoder.

paragraphs: CARE addresses safety while a language model is generating its response. Existing decoding interventions can reduce unsafe output at a substantial cost to response quality. The paper proposes a coordinated framework that detects potential problems, revises emerging text, and gives the model contextual guidance for correcting its subsequent generation.

Three components work together. A guard model monitors generation for potentially unsafe content. A token buffer supports rolling back problematic output so corrections can happen earlier with little disruption to the user. The model then produces a self-reflective critique of its previous output, and that critique becomes part of the context guiding later decoding.

The authors report that experiments achieve a better balance of safety, quality, and efficiency, with a low harmful-response rate and minimal disruption while retaining high response quality. The significance lies in combining targeted detection with revision and contextual self-correction. The reported outcome is an improved empirical trade-off, with the guard, rollback, and introspection components each serving a distinct part of the correction process.
neurips-2025-care-decoding-time-safety-a.tldr: CARE combines safety monitoring, buffered rollback, and self-reflective critiques to improve the safety-quality trade-off during language model generation.

paragraphs: Understanding interacting biological subsystems involves asking how strongly, and in which direction, they influence one another. The paper approaches this through control theory, emphasizing that influence can change with context. Linear methods cannot adequately capture the contextual effects of nonlinear dynamics, motivating a framework based on the dynamics’ Jacobian.

The Jacobian describes how changes in one part of a system affect its local evolution. The authors introduce JacobianODE, a deep learning method that directly estimates this object from time-series data using its mathematical properties. They report better estimation than existing methods on challenging dynamical systems, including high-dimensional chaos.

The framework is also applied to a multi-area recurrent neural network trained on a working memory selection task. Its sensory area gains greater control over its cognitive area during learning. The authors then use JacobianODE to manipulate the trained network’s behavior precisely. These demonstrations connect estimation of nonlinear interactions with both interpreting and controlling a learned dynamical system.
neurips-2025-characterizing-control-betw.tldr: JacobianODE estimates nonlinear interaction dynamics from time series to characterize subsystem control and manipulate a trained recurrent network.

paragraphs: Evaluating a different decision policy can require understanding the full range of outcomes it would produce. This paper introduces Counterfactual Policy Mean Embedding, or CPME, to represent that counterfactual outcome distribution in a reproducing kernel Hilbert space. This mathematical representation supports flexible distributional evaluation without imposing a parametric form on the outcome distribution.

The authors develop a plug-in estimator and a doubly robust alternative. The latter corrects for bias associated with both the outcome embedding model and the propensity model, which describes how actions were selected. Their analysis establishes improved convergence rates for this corrected estimator.

The framework also provides a doubly robust kernel statistic for hypothesis testing. Its asymptotic normality supports efficient tests and straightforward confidence intervals as sample sizes grow. CPME additionally supports sampling from the counterfactual distribution. Numerical simulations illustrate practical advantages over existing methods, bringing distribution estimation, statistical comparison, and counterfactual sampling into one framework for assessing alternative policies.
neurips-2025-doubly-robust-estimation-of.tldr: CPME uses kernel embeddings and doubly robust estimation to evaluate, compare, and sample outcome distributions under counterfactual policies.

paragraphs: Diffusion- and flow-based robot controllers often spend the same inference effort at every control step. That can waste computation on easy subtasks while leaving harder ones underserved. Difficulty-Aware Stochastic Interpolant Policy, or DA-SIP, makes the inference budget responsive to the difficulty of the current situation.

A difficulty classifier examines RGB-D observations and selects the step budget, solver variant, and whether to use ordinary or stochastic differential equation integration at each control cycle. The controller builds on stochastic interpolants, which provide a common formulation for different diffusion and flow training and inference configurations. This gives the adaptive mechanism several ways to adjust computation.

Across manipulation benchmarks, the authors report total computation time reductions of 2.6 to 4.4 times while maintaining success rates comparable to baselines that always use the maximum computation budget. These results support allocating inference effort selectively: the framework can save substantial computation in the evaluated tasks while retaining performance comparable to a consistently expensive controller.
neurips-2025-dynamic-test-time-compute-s.tldr: DA-SIP adapts robot controller inference to task difficulty, reducing reported computation time by 2.6–4.4 times with comparable task success.

paragraphs: Language models can contradict themselves across multiple stages of inference. Reflection and debate approaches seek agreement, but agreement alone can come at the expense of accuracy. This paper proposes a game-theoretic mechanism intended to improve correctness and consistency together by incorporating self-checking into the decoding process itself.

The method treats decoding as a multistage Bayesian game. Strategic interactions dynamically move toward a consensus on reliable outputs, without requiring human feedback or additional training. Because the mechanism operates during generation and is model-agnostic, the authors apply it across different language model architectures.

The reported results include a smaller LLaMA13B model outperforming the much larger PaLM540B in the cited comparison, and a 12.4% performance improvement for DeepSeek-7B on MMLU. These findings suggest that the organization of inference can materially affect performance beyond model size alone. Across the evaluated tasks, the framework supports the paper’s claim that carefully designed consensus mechanisms can strengthen self-verification while balancing accuracy with logical consistency.
neurips-2025-from-self-check-to-consensu.tldr: A Bayesian game mechanism adds self-checking and consensus to language model decoding, improving reported accuracy and consistency without additional training.

paragraphs: Graph condensation learns a much smaller graph intended to retain the information needed from a larger one. Such graphs can accelerate graph neural networks while preserving comparable predictive performance, and can support tasks such as neural architecture search. Rapid development has made consistent evaluation increasingly important, especially for node classification.

GC4NC provides a unified framework for comparing condensation methods across several dimensions. It evaluates predictive performance and efficiency alongside privacy preservation, denoising ability, usefulness for architecture search, and transferability. This broadens evaluation beyond whether a condensed graph supports accurate classification in a single setting.

The authors report that their systematic assessment yields insights into condensed graph behavior and the design choices associated with successful methods. The contribution is an evaluation framework for examining several practical properties together, making the strengths of condensation methods easier to compare. Its publicly available code also provides a common basis for subsequent evaluations and development of methods intended for broader applications.
neurips-2025-gc4nc-a-benchmark-framework.tldr: GC4NC evaluates graph condensation methods across accuracy, efficiency, privacy, denoising, architecture search, and transferability.

paragraphs: Text-to-image diffusion models can struggle to preserve a prompt’s meaning consistently while requiring many denoising steps. LABridge addresses these issues by explicitly aligning text and image representations in a shared latent space. Its central idea is to give the generation process a structured starting distribution informed by the prompt.

A Text-Image Alignment Encoder turns text into priors aligned with image latents. A mean-conditioned Ornstein–Uhlenbeck process then interpolates between these text-conditioned priors and image representations. Replacing a homogeneous Gaussian starting point with this aligned structure is intended to preserve semantic information, stabilize generation, and reduce the required denoising steps.

On standard text-to-image benchmarks, the authors report better text–image alignment metrics and competitive FID scores relative to leading diffusion baselines. Together, these findings support improved correspondence between prompts and images while retaining competitive image generation quality. The contribution connects efficiency and semantic consistency through the design of the latent process, making alignment part of how generation proceeds.
neurips-2025-labridge-textimage-latent-a.tldr: LABridge uses text-aligned latent priors and a mean-conditioned stochastic process to improve prompt alignment and reduce denoising steps.

paragraphs: Positive-unlabeled learning studies classification when the learner receives some examples labeled positive and other examples with no revealed label. The unlabeled examples do not provide an explicit negative class. This creates a statistical question about how much information the two kinds of samples must provide for learning to succeed.

Much prior work assumes that labeled positive examples follow the data distribution restricted to positives, that the overall positive-class proportion is already known, or both. This paper analyzes a wider range of settings and explicitly does not require the learner to know that class proportion in advance. That shifts the analysis toward learning with less prior information about the population.

The authors prove upper and lower bounds on the required numbers of both labeled positive and unlabeled examples. Upper bounds establish sufficient sample sizes, while lower bounds identify sample requirements that cannot generally be avoided in the analyzed settings. The contribution is a finite-sample account of statistical complexity that tracks both sources of data.
neurips-2025-learning-from-positive-and-.tldr: The paper bounds the positive and unlabeled sample sizes needed for learning without assuming the positive-class proportion is known.

paragraphs: Graph neural networks are often judged by whether connected nodes tend to share labels, a property called homophily. Yet empirical studies suggest that properly tuned models designed for homophilic graphs can work across different homophily levels. This paper investigates the theoretical tension behind that observation and develops an architecture to address it.

The analysis identifies a smoothness–generalization dilemma: increasing message-passing hops enhances smoothness at the expense of generalization. The authors connect this difficulty to complex neighborhood class distributions, particularly in higher-order homophilic neighborhoods and heterophilic neighborhoods, where noise or sparsity can induce consequential distribution shifts.

Their Inceptive Graph Neural Network, IGNN, uses three design principles to enable distinct generalization behavior at different hops and adaptive overall smoothness. Benchmarking against 30 baselines shows superior performance for IGNN and broad applicability in certain homophilic variants. The findings support examining how models combine neighborhood scales, rather than treating the graph’s homophily level alone as sufficient to determine which architecture will work well.
neurips-2025-making-classic-gnns-strong-.tldr: IGNN addresses a theoretical trade-off between message-passing smoothness and generalization to perform strongly across varying graph homophily.

paragraphs: Survival analysis models how the probability of an event changes over time. NeuralSurv introduces Bayesian uncertainty quantification into a deep survival framework, aiming to provide both flexible predictions and calibrated uncertainty about the survival function. Its nonparametric, architecture-agnostic design captures relationships between covariates and risk that can vary continuously with time.

The method uses a two-stage data-augmentation scheme with theoretical guarantees. For posterior inference, the authors develop a mean-field variational algorithm using coordinate-ascent updates that scale linearly with model size. Locally linearizing the Bayesian neural network creates a conjugate formulation, allowing every coordinate update to be calculated in closed form.

Experiments on synthetic and real-world datasets show better calibration than state-of-the-art deep survival models while matching or exceeding their ability to discriminate between outcomes. The authors particularly emphasize benefits when data are scarce. The findings suggest that Bayesian modeling can improve the reliability of survival probabilities and their uncertainty estimates without sacrificing the predictive distinctions needed for useful survival analysis.
neurips-2025-neuralsurv-deep-survival-an.tldr: NeuralSurv combines flexible deep survival modeling with efficient Bayesian inference to improve calibration and quantify uncertainty.

paragraphs: Oligonucleotide therapeutics have potential for targets that have been difficult to treat, but their safety and efficacy remain obstacles. Predictive models could help identify unsuitable compounds earlier in discovery. A practical barrier is that relevant data are scattered across experiments and use inconsistent molecular representations, making model development difficult.

OligoGym addresses this barrier with curated, standardized datasets prepared for machine learning. The collection covers multiple therapeutic modalities and endpoints. Bringing these data into a common usable form creates a basis for developing models across several kinds of oligonucleotide prediction problems.

The authors benchmark classical and deep learning methods using different molecular featurizations, model configurations, and data-splitting strategies, establishing baselines for each dataset. This makes the contribution both a data resource and a structured starting point for comparison. The paper presents it as an initial step toward a more unified framework for dataset generation and training, supporting future predictive modeling rather than claiming that the underlying safety and efficacy challenges are already resolved.
neurips-2025-oligogym-curated-datasets-a.tldr: OligoGym standardizes oligonucleotide datasets and establishes machine learning baselines to support predictive drug discovery.

paragraphs: Point cloud registration aligns three-dimensional observations, making reliable rejection of incorrect matches important. Graph-based approaches identify mutually compatible matches, but existing structural rules involve trade-offs. Cliques impose very strict constraints and are computationally difficult to find, while k-core methods use node degree and miss higher-order structures such as triangles.

PointTruss introduces the k-truss criterion, using triangle support to select inliers. A consensus voting sampling strategy first extracts a smaller structural skeleton before decomposition, improving efficiency. The method also scores the spatial distribution of inliers to balance coverage and uniformity, helping avoid selections concentrated in sparse local clusters.

Experiments on KITTI, 3DMatch, and 3DLoMatch show reported improvements over traditional and learning-based approaches across indoor and outdoor settings. The authors describe the results as state of the art. The contribution combines a richer graph compatibility criterion with efficient sampling and spatial coverage, addressing both which matches agree structurally and whether the selected matches are distributed usefully across the point cloud.
neurips-2025-pointtruss-k-truss-for-poin.tldr: PointTruss uses triangle-supported graph structure, efficient sampling, and spatial coverage scoring to improve point cloud registration.

paragraphs: Two classifiers can have similar accuracy while making different mistakes. Error consistency measures behavioral agreement in those mistakes and is used to compare models with human observers. This paper argues that reporting the metric without confidence intervals makes benchmarking conclusions unreliable because empirical error-consistency estimates can be noisy.

The authors introduce a bootstrap procedure for constructing confidence intervals and deriving significance tests. They also develop a computational model that relates error consistency to an implicit probability of one classifier copying another’s responses. This interpretation provides guidance on how many trials an experiment needs to detect behavioral differences with sufficient statistical power.

Revisiting popular NeuroAI findings, the authors find that broad behavioral differences between humans and machines remain supported, while many reported differences among deep vision models are statistically insignificant. The result changes how fine-grained model rankings should be interpreted: an observed metric difference may not establish a reliable behavioral distinction. The methodology supports both more cautious comparisons and better-powered experimental designs.
neurips-2025-quantifying-uncertainty-in-.tldr: Confidence intervals and power analysis for error consistency reveal that many reported behavioral differences between vision models lack statistical significance.

paragraphs: Generating several candidate responses can improve language model performance, but the system still needs to choose an answer. Representation consistency, or RC, augments answer frequency with information about the model’s internal activations. It can aggregate candidates produced using different prompts or sampling strategies, without requiring a particular generation procedure.

RC examines how similar the representations are across responses that lead to the same answer. Its rationale is that highly variable representations may indicate incoherent reasoning, making that answer less trustworthy despite repeated appearances. The method can use raw activations or sparse representations produced by pretrained sparse autoencoders.

Aggregation uses cached activations and lightweight similarity calculations, requiring no additional model queries. Across four open-source models and four reasoning datasets, the authors report consistent accuracy improvements, reaching up to 4% over strong test-time scaling baselines. They also find that sparse activation consistency aligns with an intuitive notion of coherent reasoning. The contribution is an additional signal for deciding which repeated answers deserve greater weight.
neurips-2025-representation-consistency-.tldr: Representation consistency improves answer aggregation by weighting repeated answers using the similarity of cached internal model activations.

paragraphs: Semantic segmentation networks produce high-dimensional, structured outputs, making robustness verification difficult to scale. Traditional probabilistic methods can become overly conservative as output dimensionality grows, yielding unnecessarily restrictive guarantees. This paper develops a data-driven verification algorithm intended to handle large segmentation models without that degree of looseness.

The approach combines sampling-based reachability analysis, which explores possible network outputs, with conformal inference. Although conformal inference is data-efficient, it can itself become conservative in high-dimensional settings. The authors introduce techniques to reduce these sources of conservatism while retaining provable probabilistic guarantees. The method is architecture-agnostic, allowing its verification strategy to apply across network designs.

Evaluations use large segmentation models on CamVid, OCTA-500, Lung_Segmentation, and Cityscapes. The authors report reliable safety guarantees with less conservatism than traditional methods. The contribution is a way to make probabilistic robustness analysis more computationally practical and informative for structured prediction, where overly broad output uncertainty can otherwise limit the usefulness of verification.
neurips-2025-scaling-data-driven-probabi.tldr: A sampling-based conformal verification method provides less conservative probabilistic robustness guarantees for large semantic segmentation networks.

paragraphs: Semi-discrete optimal transport moves a continuous source distribution onto a discrete target distribution. The paper focuses on estimating the transport map itself. Stochastic gradient methods have performed well empirically in this setting, but a theoretical guarantee for how accurately they approximate that map had remained unresolved.

The authors analyze averaged projected stochastic gradient descent and establish computational and statistical convergence guarantees. A key step is identifying a projection set that contains an objective minimizer even when the source distribution is not compactly supported. This lets the analysis accommodate source distributions whose support need not be confined to a bounded region.

Under mild source-distribution assumptions and for the stated MTW cost family, including power costs with exponent greater than one, the map estimate achieves a minimax rate of order one over the square root of the sample count. Numerical evidence supports the theory. The result connects an empirically effective solver with an optimal statistical rate in the analyzed setting.
neurips-2025-stochastic-optimization-in-.tldr: Averaged projected SGD achieves a minimax 1/√n rate for semi-discrete transport map estimation under the paper’s distribution and cost assumptions.

paragraphs: Changing a video’s lighting and textures can help transfer visual data between simulated or real environments. Maintaining a coherent appearance across frames becomes difficult for long videos with complex motion. TC-Light addresses this problem through two stages of optimization applied after an initial generative relighting pass.

The process starts with a video produced by an inflated video relighting model. Its first optimization stage adjusts an appearance embedding to align global illumination. The second optimizes a canonical representation called the Unique Video Tensor, or UVT, to align finer details of texture and lighting. This separates broad appearance alignment from detailed consistency across the video.

The authors also establish a benchmark featuring long, highly dynamic videos. Experiments show physically plausible rerendering with superior temporal coherence and low computational cost. The findings support post-optimization as a way to improve consistency in demanding video transfers, making changes to illumination and texture more stable over time while keeping the computational requirements comparatively low.
neurips-2025-tc-light-temporally-coheren.tldr: TC-Light uses two-stage post-optimization to improve lighting and texture consistency in long, dynamic rerendered videos.

paragraphs: The paper introduces Toto, a 151-million-parameter foundation model for time-series forecasting, with particular attention to multivariate observability data. Its decoder-only architecture includes adaptations for challenges in this setting. The training corpus combines observability measurements, open datasets, and synthetic data, and is four to ten times larger than those of leading time-series foundation models.

The authors also introduce BOOM, a benchmark containing 350 million observations across 2,807 real-world time series. Both the model’s observability training data and the benchmark’s observability data come exclusively from the authors’ own telemetry and internal metrics. BOOM therefore provides a substantial evaluation resource grounded in those operational measurements.

Evaluations report state-of-the-art forecasting performance on BOOM and on established general-purpose benchmarks, indicating that Toto’s reported strengths extend beyond the newly introduced benchmark. The release includes model weights, inference and evaluation code, and BOOM’s data under Apache 2.0. Together, the model and benchmark support further work on forecasting observability signals and comparing performance across broader time-series tasks.
neurips-2025-this-time-is-different-an-o.tldr: Toto pairs observability-focused forecasting adaptations with large-scale pretraining and achieves reported state-of-the-art results on BOOM and general forecasting benchmarks.

paragraphs: Multi-label data indicate which labels apply, while a label distribution expresses their relative importance. Label enhancement tries to infer the richer distribution from readily available labels. Rankings can help, but existing approaches may inadequately describe their probabilistic relationship to distributions or struggle when several labels are equally important.

PROM introduces a pairwise ranking model built around monotonicity and orderliness assumptions for ranking probabilities. The authors derive probability mass functions that are theoretically guaranteed to preserve those properties. This creates an explicit probabilistic connection between label distributions and pairwise ranking relationships, addressing the modeling deficiencies that motivate the work.

The paper then builds a generative label enhancement algorithm on PROM that directly learns a distribution predictor from multi-label data. Extensive experiments support the proposed model’s effectiveness. The contribution links a structured probabilistic account of label rankings to a practical learning method, aiming to recover graded label importance while accommodating the possibility that labels can share the same level of importance.
neurips-2025-towards-a-pairwise-ranking-.tldr: PROM models probabilistic pairwise label rankings with guaranteed orderliness and monotonicity to learn label distributions from multi-label data.

paragraphs: Actor-critic algorithms improve an acting policy while estimating its value. When a neural network parameterizes the policy, gradient updates typically make relatively gradual improvements. Greedier updates can move more aggressively toward high-value actions, but gradual policy changes can help learning remain stable. This paper addresses that trade-off by changing value estimation.

The proposed framework adds a second greedification operator used only when updating the policy’s value estimate. This lets the agent evaluate non-parameterized policies and use more aggressive improvement within value updates, while retaining steady gradient-based changes to the acting policy. The two update processes can therefore use different degrees of greediness.

The authors prove convergence within generalized policy iteration for finite-horizon problems. They also incorporate value improvement into TD3 and SAC, reporting performance that significantly improves on or matches the respective baselines across DeepMind continuous control environments. With negligible reported computation and implementation cost, the approach offers a practical way to exploit greedier value updates while preserving gradual changes in behavior.
neurips-2025-value-improved-actor-critic.tldr: Value improvement adds greedier updates to actor-critic value estimation while keeping acting-policy changes gradual, improving or matching reported TD3 and SAC performance.
